{"code": "import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Check premises

# Premise 1: email campaign targeted at high-value customers
# -> Check if email channel has higher proportion of loyal/returning customers
channel_segment = df.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
channel_segment['total'] = channel_segment.sum(axis=1)
channel_segment['loyal_ratio'] = channel_segment['loyal'] / channel_segment['total']

# Premise 2: six QA orders with revenue = 999999.99
qa_orders = df[df['revenue'] == '999999.99']
num_qa = len(qa_orders)

# Premise 3: refunded orders are included
refunded_count = df[df['status'] == 'refunded'].shape[0]

# Premise 4: channel not randomly assigned
# -> Already known from doc, but we can check if channel and segment are correlated

# Premise 5: email aimed at loyal customers who buy more
# -> Check if email has higher conversion rate, and if loyal customers have higher conversion

# Print checks
print(f"Number of QA orders: {num_qa}")
print(f"Number of refunded orders: {refunded_count}")
print(f"Channel by segment:\n{channel_segment}")

# Also check for -1 in customer_age
age_neg1 = (df['customer_age'] == -1).sum()
print(f"Number of -1 ages: {age_neg1}")"}
